references.text: The promise that five will chase a hundred and a hundred will chase ten thousand, showing God's power when the people are faithful to him.
One of you will chase a thousand, for the Lord your God fights for you, as he has promised.
Saul sold David into the hands of the Philistines, as an example of being handed over to enemies.
A thousand will flee at the threat of one man, and at the threat of five you will flee - a picture of defeat when God does not protect.
God who sells his people without payment, as an expression that he hands them over to their enemies.
You have sold your people for nothing - the same theme that God hands over his people.
The Lord's anger against Israel led him to hand them over into the hands of robbers, and he sold them to the enemies around them.
The Lord sold Israel into the hands of the king of Cushan - an example of God handing his people over to their enemies.
The Lord sold Israel into Jabin's hand - a repeated motif that God hands over the disobedient.
